examples: Say it again.
I will try again.
Let us play again.

more.def: Once more, or as it was before.
examples: The pond froze again after the warm days ended.
Read the first page again so we can hear it clearly.
I hope to visit the lake again next summer.
Put the ladder against the wall.
I sat against the tree.
The rain tapped against the window.

more.def: Pressing on or touching something for support or from the side.
examples: The bike was propped against the fence.
Waves crashed against the rocks all night.
He rested his back against the warm stone wall.
Our team plays against the blue team.
I raced against my sister.
Mom played against me at cards.

more.def: Competing with someone in a contest, or not agreeing with something.
examples: The soccer team plays against its rivals from the next town on Saturday.
Many people voted against building a loud factory near the park.
Is it against the rules to touch the ball with your hands?
What is your age?
Mia's age is seven.
Her age is eight.

more.def: The number of years that someone or something has lived or existed.
examples: At the age of six, I learned to swim.
The tree's age is over two hundred years.
Children of every age enjoyed the show.

easy.def: A very long time in the past.
examples: The Ice Age was cold.
Dinosaurs lived in a far-off age.
In the Stone Age, people used rocks as tools.

more.def: A long period of history that is known for something.
examples: People made tools of stone in the Stone Age.
Mammoths lived during the Ice Age.
We are living in the age of computers.

easy.def: An office or group that does a certain job.
examples: A travel agency helped us book.
The agency found a new home for the dog.
The agency helps people.

more.def: A business or part of a government that does a certain kind of work.
examples: A travel agency booked our trip to the beach.
The weather agency warned about the storm.
The government agency protects the forests.

easy.def: A list of things to do at a meeting.
examples: The agenda is on the board.
The agenda has three items.
Read the agenda.

more.def: A list of the things that will be talked about or done at a meeting.
examples: The agenda for the club meeting is on the board.
The first item on the agenda was the picnic.
We read the agenda before class.

easy.def: A person who helps other people with a job.
examples: The travel agent booked our trip.
My aunt is a ticket agent.
An agent helped us find a house.

more.def: A person who acts for others, or whose job is to provide a service.
examples: The travel agent booked our flights and hotel.
An agent helped the family find a new house.
A ticket agent checked our bags.

easy.def: Acting in an angry way and wanting to hurt.
examples: The dog showed aggression.
Aggression is not kind.
He used no aggression.

more.def: Angry or rough behavior toward someone, especially when it starts without a good reason.
examples: The coach talked to the player about showing aggression on the field.
The dog's aggression frightened the smaller dogs at the park.
Words are a better way to settle a problem than aggression.
The dog was aggressive.
An aggressive goose chased us.
He was an aggressive player.

more.def: Acting in an angry way and ready to attack or argue.
examples: The aggressive goose chased us across the yard.
The dog was aggressive and growled at everyone.
Do not be aggressive when you play.
The dog was agitated.
She felt agitated.
An agitated crowd.

more.def: Feeling upset, nervous or unable to stay calm.
examples: The dog was agitated by the loud thunder and paced around the room.
She felt agitated waiting for the test results.
An agitated crowd gathered when the show was delayed.

easy.def: In the past, counting back from now.
examples: I came a week ago.
It was long ago.
She left an hour ago.

more.def: Back in the past from the present time.
examples: Dinosaurs lived millions of years ago.
My grandparents moved here fifty years ago.
The rain stopped just a few minutes ago.
The tooth was in agony.
He was in agony.
She felt agony.
He was in agony after he hurt his ankle.
The tooth gave her great agony all night.
She waited in agony for the test results.

easy.def: To think the same thing as someone else.
examples: We both agree that pizza is yummy.
Do you agree that dogs are fun?
We agree to take turns.

more.def: To have the same opinion as someone, or to say yes to something.
examples: Everyone agreed that the park was the best place for the picnic.
The two teams agreed on the rules before the game began.
I agree with you that we should leave early.

easy.def: Pleasant and easy to get along with.
examples: She is agreeable.
An agreeable day.
He was agreeable.

more.def: Pleasant and ready to agree, or enjoyable.
examples: She is an agreeable girl who is easy to get along with.
We had an agreeable day at the park.
He was agreeable to the plan and said yes.

easy.def: When people think the same or make a promise.
examples: We came to an agreement.
They have an agreement.
We reached an agreement.

more.def: A promise or a decision that two or more people have made together.
examples: We came to an agreement about who goes first.
The two teams signed an agreement.
The agreement says we will share the cost.
